::: {.lede}
Three open questions and two abstracts already published. What the open
questions share is not a method but a subject, how a brain weighs what it
already believes against what it is currently being told.
:::

## Open {.k-head}

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
Residency thesis &middot; BAP04-B-2026-6538 &middot; [in preparation]{.status .pending}
:::
### [Belief updating and sensory attenuation in schizophrenia](belief-updating-schizophrenia.qmd){.title}

Whether delusions track a failure of belief revision, a failure to attenuate
self-generated sensation, or both. A beads task and a force-matching task in
the same people.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
Theory &middot; [in design]{.status .pending}
:::
### [Akathisia as active inference](akathisia-active-inference.qmd){.title}

Akathisia drives movement that rarely settles it, and the felt and the seen
halves of the syndrome can come apart entirely. Whether active inference
explains that better than the receptor does.
:::

::: {.entry}
::: {.meta}
With the Department of Neurology &middot; [in collection]{.status .live}
:::
### [Effort and reward in multiple sclerosis](effort-ms.qmd){.title}

Fatigue and depression overlap on every questionnaire that tries to tell them
apart. An effort-based task can ask instead whether the cost of acting or the
value of the outcome is what changed.
:::
